modv0.1.1

meterOne quiet line for the session's numbers.

Context, rate-limit windows, cost and the prompt cache, each marked measured or estimated, with a band only when a figure crosses a line.

At the prompt of a terminal session:

/plugin install meter --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills
Other ways to install

  • From a shell:

    claude plugin install meter --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills

  • In the desktop app: click + next to the prompt box, then Plugins, Add marketplace with LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills, then Add plugin.

Read checkpointing-long-runs Source on GitHub

Commands

CommandWhat it does
/meterevery figure, where it came from, and the cache lifetime
/meter quietkeep the status line and silence the band for this session
/meter loudbring the band back

In use

The status line reads like ctx 41% · 5h 62% · wk 18% · $1.84. Only units with a reading appear, so a session with no cost figure shows no cost, and a figure is never shown as zero when it is missing.

The mod registers no tool for the model and never writes to the conversation. It informs you, and what to do about a number stays yours.

How it behaves

  • Readings. The host pushes a new reading when a figure moves, and the mod reads once at start. Nothing polls.
  • The band. It shows a line when context reaches 80%, when a rate-limit window reaches 80% or 95%, or when the cache is probably cold. A line is announced once per crossing, and again only after its figure falls 5 points below the line and crosses it again. A 95% crossing replaces the 80% one for the same window. When several lines are showing, the newest is drawn and the rest are counted. Hide hides the current lines until the next crossing. Under 60 columns the band uses a short form.
  • Cold cache. This is an estimate. The cache counts as cold when the session has been idle longer than the cache lifetime with at least 50,000 tokens of context. It is recomputed when you start a draft and when you send, and once by a timer when the lifetime runs out. It never delays a send.
  • Cache lifetime. It starts at 5 minutes, labelled assumed. If the first request of a turn of at least 50,000 input tokens comes after more than 5 minutes idle and reads more than half of its input from the cache, the lifetime becomes 60 minutes, labelled observed. If a turn comes after less than the current lifetime and writes at least 90% of its input fresh, it goes back to 5 minutes. This is an inference from two numbers and can be wrong.
  • Limits. Rate-limit readings come from this session's own responses, so usage spent elsewhere shows after this session's next reply. Off a subscription there are no windows. Nothing here keeps the cache warm, because a ping spends tokens and how cached reads count against plan limits is not documented. The band draws only where the host draws a band above the prompt.
